standard_prerequisites: Same chapter: theorem-inifinite-galois-theory context of transcendence bases (delivered card L48327: transcendence degree of finitely generated extensions), lemma-purely-transcendental-degree (same chapter: [k'(x_1..x_r) : k(x_1..x_r)] = [k':k] for purely transcendental towers); standard fact used as the closing step: an algebraic extension whose finite subextensions have uniformly bounded degree is finite (a strict chain grows the degree by at least 2 per step)
core_obligations: Fix a transcendence basis x_1..x_r; then n = [K : k(x_1..x_r)] < infinity

For a finite subextension k'/k inside K, base change along the rational function field gives [k'(x_1..x_r) : k(x_1..x_r)] = [k' : k] (lemma-purely-transcendental-degree), and k'(x_1..x_r) sits inside K, so [k' : k] <= n
Bounded degrees of finite subextensions of the algebraic closure of k in K force that closure to be finite over k
proof_roadmap: Bound finite subextensions by the degree over the rational function field
Conclude finiteness from the uniform degree bound
